definitions.gloss: by force; by brute strength; forcibly
definitions.explanation: Relying on physical strength or coercive power rather than reason, negotiation, or skill. Almost always used in the pattern {力|ちから}ずくで (by force).

examples.japanese: {力|ちから}ずくで{扉|とびら}を{開|あ}けた。
{力|ちから}ずくで{連|つ}れて{行|い}かれた。
examples.english: I was taken away by force.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}を{力|ちから}ずくで{解決|かいけつ}しようとしても、{相手|あいて}の{反発|はんぱつ}を{招|まね}くだけだ。
examples.english: Even if you try to resolve problems by force, you will only provoke resistance from the other party.

notes:
Used almost exclusively in the pattern {力|ちから}ずくで (by force, using brute strength). Contrasts with {話|はな}し{合|あ}い (discussion) or {説得|せっとく} (persuasion) as a means to an end.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {力|ちから}ずくで: by force, forcibly
- {力|ちから}ずくで{連|つ}れて{行|い}く: to take someone by force
- {力|ちから}ずくで{押|お}しつける: to force something on someone

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {強引|ごういん}に: forcibly, pushily — often implies social pressure rather than physical force
- {無理|むり}やり: by force, against one's will — more colloquial, focuses on the lack of consent
